## Natural history notes

A large aquatic insect characterized by long smoky wings held roof-like over the body, long antennae, and a soft brown to grayish body. In Florida, it is found near ponds, lakes, marshes, swamps, slow streams, and other freshwater wetlands where the aquatic larvae can develop. Adults are short-lived and often come to lights near water, while the larvae live in aquatic habitats as predators, feeding on small invertebrates and helping transfer energy from freshwater systems to birds, bats, fish, and other predators.
